question: A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at a certain rate of compound interest. In how many years will it be sixteen times at the same rate?
solution:
**Given:**

2P = P[1 + R/100]⁵

**Formula used:**

A = P x [1 + (R /100)]T

A = CI + P

here, 

A = Amount

CI = Compound Interest

P = Principle

R = Rate

T = Time

**Solution:**

2P = P[1 + R/100]⁵

⇒ 2¹/⁵ = (1 + R/100)

Now,

16P = P[1+R/100]T

⇒ 16 = [21/5]T

⇒ 16 = 2T/⁵

⇒ 2⁴ = 2T/⁵

⇒ 4 = T /5

T = 20

**Henc, after 20 years, the amount will be 16 times the principle.**
